json.title: E2: Per-tenant event ingestion quota (100k/day, durable Postgres counter)

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent

json.body:
## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Enforce a per-tenant daily event ingestion cap using a durable Postgres counter, replacing the in-memory rate limiter for the hosted deployment path only.

**Depends on:** #44 (E1 — needs `tenant_id`/`withTenant` plumbing in place).

**Current behavior:**
The existing rate limiter (`isRateLimited()`) uses an in-memory `Map`. This works for self-hosted (single, long-running process) but is not a real limit in a serverless deployment — a cold-start invocation has fresh memory, so the counter does not actually accumulate state across invocations. There is no per-tenant event volume cap anywhere in the codebase, and no cost-recovery mechanism exists (v1.0 has no billing), so nothing currently stops one tenant from consuming unbounded shared infrastructure.

**Desired behavior:**
A `tenant_quotas` table (`tenant_id`, `events_today INTEGER DEFAULT 0`, `quota_date DATE DEFAULT CURRENT_DATE`, `events_daily_cap INTEGER DEFAULT 100000`) tracks each tenant's daily event count. Inside the event-ingestion path, in the same transaction as the event insert (via `withTenant`):
1. If `quota_date < CURRENT_DATE`: reset `events_today = 0`, `quota_date = CURRENT_DATE`, atomically.
2. If `events_today >= events_daily_cap`: reject with HTTP 429 and a `Retry-After` header (seconds remaining until UTC midnight) — before the event is written.
3. Otherwise: insert the event and increment `events_today` atomically, in the same transaction.

The self-hosted deployment path keeps the existing in-memory limiter unchanged (it works correctly there — single process, memory persists between requests). The hosted deployment path uses this Postgres-counter implementation instead, behind the same `isRateLimited()`-shaped interface, selected by environment — this should read as a drop-in alternate implementation, not a rewrite of the self-hosted behavior.

The cap (`events_daily_cap`) is visible to the founder in Settings/Dashboard as "X / 100,000 events today" — never a silent wall.

A separate, lower-frequency mechanism (not part of the hot ingestion path) sums `events_today` across all tenants and compares it to a known fraction of the hosted Postgres provider's plan-level compute capacity, logging/emailing an alert if crossed. This is a monitoring signal for a human decision (pause signups, upgrade plan), not an automatic per-request action.

**Key interfaces:**
- `tenant_quotas` table schema as above
- The event-ingestion function's tenant + quota-aware extension (the existing `processEvent()`-shaped seam)
- `events_daily_cap` must be adjustable per-tenant without a code deploy (it's a plain column, not a compiled constant)
- The aggregate monitor — a scheduled job, reusing whatever scheduling mechanism the deployment already has for keep-alive pings (see #42/H1)

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] An event under quota is accepted and `events_today` increments by exactly one
- [ ] An event at exactly `events_daily_cap` is accepted; the next one for that tenant is rejected
- [ ] A rejected event returns HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header equal to seconds remaining until UTC midnight
- [ ] The quota resets correctly across a UTC-day boundary
- [ ] Two tenants with different `events_daily_cap` values are limited independently and correctly
- [ ] Self-hosted deployment continues to use the existing in-memory limiter, unmodified in behavior
- [ ] The founder-visible quota indicator reflects the real counter value
- [ ] The aggregate monitor alert fires when total ingestion crosses the configured threshold (test with a mocked/lowered threshold)

**Out of scope:**
- Any billing or paid-tier logic
- Redis, Upstash, or any external rate-limiting service — this stays entirely in Postgres
- Session replay's separate storage quota (see E4)
